subject.title: fix: harden small runtime and installer edge cases

question: Should this maintainer batch land with the 1 MiB ClawRouter usage cap, the shared 16 MiB CDP JSON cap, and stricter Arch detection as written?
rationale: The patch appears mechanically sound, but the response caps and installer detection change are compatibility choices that green unit tests cannot decide for existing unusual deployments.

options.title: Land With These Boundaries
options.body: Accept the capped-response and stricter distro-detection behavior as the intended hardening tradeoff once required checks finish.

options.title: Tune Compatibility First
options.body: Adjust the ClawRouter cap, CDP cap, or Arch detection fallback before merge if maintainers know of real deployments outside the new assumptions.

options.title: Split The Batch
options.body: Pause this aggregate PR and land the source fixes separately if maintainers want independent risk decisions for each edge case.

recommendation.title: Land With These Boundaries
recommendation.body: Accept the capped-response and stricter distro-detection behavior as the intended hardening tradeoff once required checks finish.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the replacement batch and has the clearest cross-surface signal for accepting or tuning the compatibility tradeoff.
